title: Hydroxyurea in sickle cell disease: increases fetal hemoglobin (HbF) synthesis
vignette: A 23-year-old woman with a history of sickle cell disease comes to the office for follow-up. The patient is homozygous for hemoglobin S and has had frequent episodes of painful vasoocclusive crises. She has no other medical conditions and takes folic acid supplementation. The patient does not use tobacco, alcohol, or illicit drugs. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Additional therapy with hydroxyurea is planned. This medication is likely to improve this patient's symptoms primarily through which of the following mechanisms?

clues.note: Homozygous HbS (sickle cell disease) causes hemoglobin polymerization when deoxygenated, leading to hemolysis and vasoocclusive crises.

clues.text: frequent episodes of painful vasoocclusive crises
clues.note: Recurrent vasoocclusive crises are the target of hydroxyurea therapy, which reduces their frequency.
Hydroxyurea increases synthesis of FETAL hemoglobin (HbF), which does not sickle and dilutes HbS, reducing polymerization and crises.

whatMatters: HYDROXYUREA improves sickle cell disease primarily by INCREASING FETAL HEMOGLOBIN (HbF) synthesis. HbF lacks beta chains (unaffected by the sickle mutation) and dilutes HbS, reducing polymerization/sickling, hemolysis, vasoocclusive crises, and transfusion need. Answer D.
strategy: Recall hydroxyurea's key benefit in sickle cell disease: shifts globin production toward GAMMA chains -> more HbF (which resists sickling). Reject decreased RBC dehydration (Gardos channel blockers), direct inhibition of HbS polymerization (voxelotor, which binds the alpha chain), increased HbA2 (delta chains - not the hydroxyurea effect), increased antioxidant levels (L-glutamine), and stimulation of RBC production (would raise HbS and could worsen crises; hydroxyurea actually inhibits ribonucleotide reductase and is myelosuppressive).

options.text: Direct inhibition of red blood cell polymerization
Increased red blood cell antioxidant levels
Stimulation of red blood cell production

eliminations.label: Decreased RBC dehydration - Gardos channel blocker
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: preventing erythrocyte dehydration via the calcium-dependent (Gardos) potassium channel. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: blocking that channel could reduce dehydration but is not hydroxyurea's mechanism and hasn't been shown to improve symptoms. ✅ Correct if: a Gardos channel inhibitor.

eliminations.label: Direct inhibition of HbS polymerization - voxelotor
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: directly preventing HbS polymerization by binding the alpha chain (voxelotor) to increase oxygen affinity. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: that is voxelotor's mechanism; hydroxyurea works INDIRECTLY by raising HbF. ✅ Correct if: voxelotor therapy.

eliminations.label: Increased HbA2 - delta chains, not hydroxyurea
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: raising hemoglobin A2 (alpha2-delta2). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: hydroxyurea increases GAMMA-globin (HbF), not delta-globin (HbA2). ✅ Correct if: a therapy increasing delta-globin expression.

eliminations.label: Increased antioxidant levels - L-glutamine
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: reducing oxidative stress in RBCs (L-glutamine, a glutathione precursor). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: that is L-glutamine's mechanism, used when hydroxyurea is not tolerated - not hydroxyurea's action. ✅ Correct if: L-glutamine therapy.

eliminations.label: Stimulation of RBC production - would worsen sickling
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: increasing erythrocyte production (e.g., erythropoietin). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: more RBCs would raise HbS and could worsen crises; hydroxyurea actually INHIBITS ribonucleotide reductase (myelosuppressive) and benefits patients via HbF, not by stimulating erythropoiesis. ✅ Correct if: erythropoietin-stimulating agent.

reasoning: Sickle cell disease (homozygous HbS) causes HbS polymerization, hemolysis, and vasoocclusive crises
Hydroxyurea shifts globin synthesis toward gamma chains, raising fetal hemoglobin (HbF)
HbF does not sickle and dilutes HbS, reducing polymerization and crises
-> increased fetal hemoglobin synthesis; answer D
mechanism: SICKLE CELL DISEASE results from a missense mutation in the beta-globin gene (valine for glutamic acid at position 6), producing HEMOGLOBIN S (HbS). When deoxygenated or dehydrated, HbS POLYMERIZES, deforming red cells into sickled shapes that hemolyze and occlude small vessels (painful VASOOCCLUSIVE CRISES, ischemia). HYDROXYUREA, an antimetabolite that inhibits ribonucleotide reductase (myelosuppressive), also shifts globin gene transcription from the beta locus toward the GAMMA-globin locus, INCREASING circulating FETAL HEMOGLOBIN (HbF, alpha2-gamma2). Because HbF lacks beta chains, it is UNAFFECTED by the sickle mutation and does not participate in polymerization; raising HbF DILUTES HbS and RAISES the threshold for sickling, thereby reducing hemolysis, vasoocclusive crises, and transfusion requirements. The distractors are other (or incorrect) mechanisms: Gardos channel blockade (RBC dehydration), voxelotor (direct anti-polymerization via alpha-chain binding), HbA2/delta-globin, L-glutamine (antioxidant), and erythropoiesis stimulation (which would increase HbS).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Heme/Pharm > sickle cell disease: HbS polymerizes when deoxygenated -> hemolysis/vasoocclusion; hydroxyurea increases HbF (gamma globin), reducing crises; also inhibits ribonucleotide reductase (myelosuppressive); voxelotor/L-glutamine are alternatives.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Hydroxyurea raises fetal hemoglobin (HbF), which resists sickling and dilutes HbS.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on hemoglobin S, fetal hemoglobin (HbF), vasoocclusive crisis, hydroxyurea, or ribonucleotide reductase? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Voxelotor = direct anti-polymerization; L-glutamine = antioxidant; Gardos blocker = dehydration; HbA2 = delta chains; EPO would raise HbS.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: hydroxyurea increases HbF in sickle cell disease -> fewer vasoocclusive crises (also myelosuppressive via ribonucleotide reductase).

keywords.back: Lacks beta chains -> doesn't sickle; dilutes HbS
Binds HbS alpha chain -> inhibits polymerization (increases O2 affinity)
Antioxidant (reduces oxidative stress) in sickle cells

firstAid.detail: Pharm: increases HbF -> fewer vasoocclusive crises.

memoryHook: Hydroxyurea turns the 'fetal' hemoglobin switch back on - HbF can't sickle, so it dilutes the bad HbS and the painful crises ease up.
